title: Free-variable bound on the leftover path
statement: Let $\rho_0$ and $\sigma$ be restrictions on $n$ variables, let $L$ be a list of literals each paired with its position index in a clause, and let $P$ be a decision-tree path (a list of variable–direction pairs). Suppose the length of $P$ is at most the number of free variables of $\rho_0$. Write $(P', \rho_0', \sigma', A)$ for the result of processing $L$ against $P$ starting from $\rho_0$ and $\sigma$, so that $P'$ is the remaining path and $\rho_0'$ the updated first restriction. Then the length of $P'$ is at most the number of free variables of $\rho_0'$.
